MINUTES

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to

and Planning Commissions.

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the public hearing on the
  project approvals; 2) Take public testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; 4) Close
  the public hearing on the project approvals; 5) Adopt Resolution No. 2382
  adopting a Mitigated Negative Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring and
  Reporting Program for the Project; 6) Adopt Resolution No. 2383 approving
  Tentative Parcel Map No. 7239800 a two-lot subdivision, consisting of a 1.48-
  acre parcel (Parcel 1) and a 1.65-acre parcel (Parcel 2), with commercial
  condominiums on Parcel 2 and Grading Permit for Project-related grading; 7)
  Adopt Resolution No. 2384 approving Variances, Conditional Use Permit, and a
  Precise Plan of Design for the Parcel 1 of Tentative Parcel Map No. 72398; and
  8) Adopt Resolution No. 2385 approving Variances, Conditional Use Permit,
  and a Precise Plan of Design for the Parcel 2 of Tentative Parcel Map No. 72398.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 27, 2016
   Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  Discussion took place in response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL’S question
  regarding air space rights.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  Alex Rose, Continental Development Corporation, thanked staff, in particular,
  Planning Director Wahba, Senior Planner Naughton, former Principal Planner
  Wetzel, and Peninsula Center Library District Director Kathy Gould, for their work
  on bringing this project to the COUNCIL.

  Mr. Rose then provided an extensive overview of the project. He addressed several
  COUNCIL questions regarding ownership opportunities for those businesses who
  want to invest in the community and clarified the question of air space rights,
  noting that there will not be any buildings on the parking structure.

  Ryan Leong, SRM Development, noted that Bill Petit, President, Merrill Gardens,
  could not attend the meeting due to a personal matter, but would be open to
  meeting with the COUNCIL if desired. He then provided additional background on
  his firm and their intention to provide a healthy lifestyle for senior housing.

  Chad Lorenz, Urbal Architecture, noted his pleasure in working with staff and
  provided a detailed overview of the project and its amenities.

  Mr. Rose addressed the question of condominium style ownership of the
  commercial units, indicating that he does not foresee any need for redevelopment
  in the future once this project is constructed. He then addressed commercial
  benefit of the project and the synergy with the Library and the Peninsula Seniors
  organization.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Mr. Rose noted that there will be up
  to 13 individual condominiums depending on the size of the units within the
  commercial building.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Lorenz noted that the windows will be
  recessed.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Lorenz noted that the height elevation
  on Silver Spur Road will be shifted back from the street.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that the most important issue was the
  Library parking and was pleased to know that this situation was resolved. Mr.
  Rose commented that the credit for coming up with a solution for the Library
  parking goes to Planning Director Wahba.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN regarding residents’ concerns with
  the loss of retail space, Mr. Rose noted the current vacancy rates for retail and
  indicated that residents, staff and visitors will purchase goods and services in the
  commercial district.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN suggested reviewing the width of the sidewalk
  because there is not one on the other side.  He further questioned the
  massiveness of the building, and asked if anything can be done to make the
  sidewalk more “walkable.” Mr. Lorenz noted that there is a five foot setback from
  the building which will have terraced planters to provide a buffer and a canopy.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN then suggested subtracting three feet of private space to
  enlarge the public walking space.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that wider sidewalks have been her concern
  for many years.

  Mr. Lorenz responded that a wider sidewalk could be accommodated.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 27, 2016
   MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that the public benefit would likely outweigh
  code requirements in the event that providing the additional walk space infringed
  on the private property regulations.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF referred to the Merrill Gardens project in Huntington
  Beach indicating that that particular building is very imposing. Mr. Lorenz
  responded that the building is similar, but there are substantial differences in the
  surrounding development which make that building stand out, and opined that
  the building in Rolling Hills Estates should blend in with its surroundings.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN wanted to make sure that the Merrill Gardens’
  signs state Rolling Hills Estates and not Rolling Hills. Mr. Lorenz noted that this
  will be corrected.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ asked Mr. Leong about the statistics for senior
  housing, how recently this information was gathered, and if the information
  included the new senior developments surrounding the City.  Mr. Leong
  responded that all existing and planned projects were included in the projections.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL inquired about the traffic study at the signalized
  intersections and asked if unsignalized intersections were considered. Senior
  Planner Naughton noted that the traffic studies review both signalized and
  unsignalized intersections and the ones chosen by the Traffic Engineer were
  appropriate for this project.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Anjum Bawa, Traffic Engineer, Fehr &
  Peers, noted that Crenshaw Boulevard and Palos Verdes Drive North were
  evaluated against the capacity utilizing the City’s criteria. Senior Planner
  Naughton noted that the study was conducted between 4:00-5:45 p.m.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that the proposed project should reduce traffic
  overall.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN asked Mr. Rose if Continental Development has commercial
  condominiums in other cities. Mr. Rose noted that in El Segundo they have a 15-
  acre site containing 15 buildings.

  John Polen, PV Premier Bank, commented that it is a great project and will give
  many businesses a reason to own property in the City. He further noted that he
  served on the Chamber of Commerce’s economic committee and this is a great
  commitment to the Peninsula as well as other businesses and encouraged the
  City to work with the developer to solve any issues.

  Hank Parker, Vice Chair, Economic Development, PVP Chamber of Commerce,
  noted that some comments from prospective businesses were concerned about
  the amount of foot traffic coming in, but with the increase in residents and staff
  from this project, could inspire landlords to improve their own properties.

  Eileen Hupp, President/CEO, PVP Chamber of Commerce, noted her strong
  support for this project as it will generate additional economic activity. She noted
  that the community is excited to have a world class development investing in the
  community, and on behalf of the Chamber Board of Directors and 400
  businesses, she urged the COUNCIL to support this project as presented.

  Ann Shaw, President, Peninsula Seniors, commented on her excitement about
  this project and hoped the COUNCIL would approve the proposal. She noted that
  the Peninsula Seniors’ plan is to lease and purchase a portion of Parcel B because
  it is a perfect location for a senior center. She noted that the Peninsula Seniors
  have a wonderful relationship with Merrill Gardens.

  Mark Smith, Malaga Bank, noted that this project will revitalize this location and
  recommended approval of the project.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 27, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that the renderings are beautiful and
  appreciated the professionalism associated with this project. She further noted
  her appreciation of the demand for senior housing. and her preference for
  recreational/shopping opportunities for young families in the commercial district.
  She voiced concern that commercial space is being eliminated, but indicated that
  she would support the project.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that she also had concerns because years
  ago the COUNCIL had envisioned a walking area with an enhanced commercial
  district along the Brickwalk. Unfortunately, in spite of the Mixed Use Overlay
  Zone, the commercial center has not become a retail destination. She further
  noted her appreciation regarding the parking issue and the good relationship
  between Merrill Gardens, Peninsula Seniors and Peninsula Center Library.
  Finally she noted that the staff report does provide the findings to make a
  mitigated negative declaration on the environmental impact report.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted her excitement for this project as it provides
  exciting opportunities for seniors. She further noted that the audience turn out
  shows the COUNCIL there is support for this project.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that the City is looking to have quality
  developers in the City. He then offered his thanks to the community and hoped to
  energize this location with this development.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN concurred with COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL’S comments
  and congratulated the Applicants for their patience in working with the Library as
  well as the Library for working with the developer on the very important parking
  issue. He noted that this project is unique and will be interested to see how the

B.  LANDSCAPE CONSULTANT SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve a General Fund capital
  improvement project budget amendment of $72,360 for street median and City
  Hall grounds landscape improvement consulting services; and 2) Approve the
  professional services agreement with MIG for street median and City Hall
  landscape project design services for improvements to the City's street medians
  and City Hall grounds.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted her recollection that this item was going to start
  with a smaller area. City Manager Prichard noted that the COUNCIL authorized
  negotiating a scope of service at the last COUNCIL meeting which looked at all
  the medians as well as the City Hall grounds.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that the idea behind these services was to
  create a comprehensive plan and take into consideration what would be
  suitable for the climate in all the medians and City Hall.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted her understanding that the City was to receive
  input from the neighborhoods impacted by these medians.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that the consultants would be holding
  community meetings and receive input from the affected neighborhoods.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted her concern with moving forward on this project
  due to the cost.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted his concern in creating expectations that might not
  be able to be met and suggested possibly making this part of the General Plan.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that SCAG is providing sustainable grants
  that may include applications for median landscaping projects.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that this could be made part of the Conservation
  Element in the General Plan. COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ commented that this
  would be appropriate.

  City Manager Prichard suggested tabling this item and having the
  subcommittee and Park and Activities Commission review the medians at the
  west end of the City.
